verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya *IPE Study Material for Jr. Students* 2026-27 edition, physics volume, Chapter 9 Very Short Answer Question 10 (printed p.98). Only the question was taken; the answer, its steps and its mark split are original work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. The 1 + 1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Physics hand-checked: compressibility K is the reciprocal of bulk modulus, K = 1/B = −(ΔV/V)/ΔP; the minus sign makes K positive because volume decreases (ΔV negative) as pressure increases (ΔP positive).

insider_note: Dropping the minus sign in K = −(ΔV/V)/ΔP is the single most common way this mark is lost, even when the rest of the definition is correct.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Definition
lines: Compressibility K is the reciprocal of the
steps.margin_note: State both the words 'reciprocal of bulk modulus' and the symbol relation K = 1/B — either alone is incomplete.
steps.why: Compressibility is defined as the reciprocal of bulk modulus so that a material that is easy to compress (small B) has a large K, and a material that resists compression (large B) has a small K.
common_mistakes: Writing K = B instead of K = 1/B.
Confusing compressibility with strain, which has no reciprocal relation to B.
steps.memory_tip: Compressibility and bulk modulus are opposites: K = 1/B.

steps.label: Formula with the minus sign
lines: It is the fractional decrease in volume
steps.margin_note: The minus sign is part of the formula, not decoration — omitting it can cost this mark.
steps.why: The minus sign is there because volume decreases as pressure increases, so ΔV is negative for a positive ΔP; the minus sign makes K itself come out as a positive quantity.
common_mistakes: Dropping the minus sign — without it K would come out negative, which is not physically meaningful.
Writing ΔP/ΔV instead of ΔV/ΔP in the fraction.
steps.memory_tip: Pressure up, volume down — the minus sign turns that decrease into a positive K.
